@gjsify/adwaita-react-native.note: Adwaita widgets with ONE API surface and two implementations — the real Adw.* widget on GTK4 through @gjsify/gtk-host, React Native primitives over @gjsify/adwaita-core's arithmetic on a phone. Direction B to @gjsify/react-native's direction A, and the second dialect ADR 0032's `What this does not decide` asks for. Two containers (Bin, Clamp) plus four groups — the window chrome (ToolbarView, HeaderBar, WindowTitle, WrapBox, StatusPage), the content and feedback widgets (Avatar, Banner, Spinner, ButtonContent, ToastOverlay), the boxed-list rows (Action, Button, Switch, Entry, Expander) and the preferences group with the three rows that live in one (PreferencesPage, PreferencesGroup, Combo, Spin, PasswordEntry) — each carrying the whole vertical rather than a wide widget set; the count is derived into the STATUS.md matrix and not asserted here. The rows re-implement nothing: every derivation they share — `string_is_not_empty` on both labels, `Adw.EntryRow`'s `update_empty` truth table and its apply latch, character-counted truncation, the switch row's two routes into one transition, the expander's disclosure — is `@gjsify/adwaita-core`'s, the same call `@gjsify/adwaita-web` and `@gjsify/adwaita-nativescript` make, while the GTK half calls none of it and is the oracle instead. The preferences group is the same shape one level up: `derivePreferencesGroupHeader` answers in one call what `update_title_visibility`, `update_description_visibility`, `update_header_visibility`, `is_single_line` and `update_listbox_visibility` answer in five C functions, and `ComboState`/`SpinState`/`PasswordEntryRowState` carry the selection, the clamp and the peek pair. Two properties keep libadwaita's NAME and take the core's type because the libadwaita type cannot cross this surface — `AdwComboRow:model` is a `Gio.ListModel` and `AdwSpinRow:adjustment` is a `Gtk.Adjustment` — and both are memoised on their CONTENT, since gtk-host writes a property only when the prop changes and a freshly constructed one would take the selection or the value back to what was authored. `Adw.ExpanderRow`'s placement policy was curated INTO `@gjsify/gtk-host` by this package: it was in the generated table, which knows the tag and no placement, so every child of an `<adw-expander-row>` was an `uncurated-placement` refusal — and curating it needed the `slotted` policy to grow the per-slot `wrapSlots` that `indexed` already declared for `Gtk.ListBox`, because `gtk_list_box_remove` does not unwrap the implicit `GtkListBoxRow` an inner list makes for a non-row child and the child leaks on unmount behind one Gtk-WARNING (measured, GTK 4.22.4; caught by the host's own slotted round-trip mechanism). The halves are selected by the `exports` map's `react-native` condition, with every barrel naming its platform files literally rather than relying on a resolver to pick a sibling; the base modules refuse by name for a tool that honours neither mechanism. scripts/check-adwaita-rn-platform-split.mjs holds both platform modules, the exports map (condition ORDER included), the three barrels and the per-file @jsxImportSource pragma, and carries the metro-resolver measurements the design rests on. Both halves are held to ONE declared surface by tsc (parity.spec.ts), by prop NAME SET rather than assignability, because every prop is optional and structural assignability accepts a rename between two such types; the GTK half is photographed through gtk-host's shotEvidence at two frame widths, one of them inside the easing region where a min() approximation diverges, and the React Native half runs on React's own reconciler against a react-native double type-pinned to the real surface and asserts the same two pairs as style objects.
@gjsify/adwaita-react-native.missing: Everything past the four groups — the six remaining adaptive ones (BreakpointBin, both split views, ViewStack, ViewSwitcher and its bar), the lists and the dialogs. `Adw.PreferencesPage` is here without its `GtkScrolledWindow` on React Native and without `banner`, and `Adw.PreferencesGroup` without `header-suffix` and `separate-rows`; the preferences DIALOG is not. No Yoga and no device: the React Native half is type-checked and tree-checked and has never run on a phone, so `width: 400` is asserted as an instruction, never as a measured pixel. The named divergences are carried in the README rather than smoothed over — AdwClamp passes childMin/childNat as 0 because React Native has no measure pass, the small/medium/large size class has no React Native sink, Adw.ClampScrollable has no counterpart by design, no icon-name prop is on the surface at all because there is no React Native icon renderer, `add_prefix` has no counterpart, AdwExpanderRow carries no enable-expansion because the rule tying it to the disclosure lives in no shared place yet, and the row THEME (padding, type scale, dim-label colour, separator) is deliberately unmapped. The property range is NOT one of them: both halves run @gjsify/adwaita-core's normalizeClampSize, because GObject gives one authored value three answers (construction stores NaN as 0, set_property refuses it, a negative keeps the previous value and logs a critical on both paths). No npm publish yet: a new name needs the manual first-publish plus Trusted Publisher bootstrap.

@gjsify/gtk-host.missing: 138 of the 164 generated widgets carry `children: { kind: 'uncurated' }` — creatable, settable and handler-bearing, but inserting a child raises `uncurated-placement` naming the tag that needs a policy. Counting only widgets that can hold a child at all, that is 79 of 101 containers; the curated 26 already cover the hard ones (AdwHeaderBar, GtkListBox, GtkStack, GtkGrid, AdwPreferencesGroup). Two measured placement defects are open (`status/open-todos.md`): inserting into an ADOPTED composite is off by one because the composite's own internal child counts as `foreign[0]`, and removing an element child does not restate displaced text. Both build halves now exist: `@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-solid` compiles JSX with `generate: "universal"` and `@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-vue` compiles `.vue` SFCs through `@vue/compiler-sfc`, each with a showcase that asserts the resulting widget tree. Tree-SHAPE reconciliation is not in the shared vector table: `patch` re-renders one shape with new props and text, so `v-if`, `<For>` and keyed reorders stay in each adapter's own spec, where the identity assertions belong. The React JSX surface has no half in `scripts/check-type-surfaces.mjs` — its element list is covered through the shared `WidgetPropsByTag`, its own `Element`/`ElementType`/`IntrinsicAttributes`/`Ref` plumbing is not. `<Teleport>` with a string target throws rather than resolving a widget by name. Non-widget attachment (controllers, adjustments, buffers, menu models) and the `model` policy for Gtk.ListView/ColumnView factories are not implemented — the generated table holds GtkWidget descendants only, so those are not yet nameable as tags.
@gjsify/gtk-host.note: Framework-agnostic GTK4/Adwaita host (ADR 0027) plus its three framework adapters. Host: shadow node tree (element/text/anchor) with `attached` as the separate fact of whether GTK has taken a node, 14 ops + 4 navigators + the isText predicate, eight child-placement policy kinds dispatched on the policy's own kind, ParamSpec-coerced properties where every silent failure is refused by name (string enum nicks resolved — GObject drops them silently through both set_property and the JS setter), signal ledger checked against the class, construct-only rebuild, eager destroy. Nothing is recorded before GTK accepts it, and containers that can only append rotate their tail rather than claim a cheap reorder. Descriptor table for GTK4 + libadwaita: 26 curated placement rules merged with 164 rows generated from the GIR (ADR 0028), one-way by shape so the generator can only ADD a gtype, never contradict a curated rule; held to the installed typelib by `descriptorProblems()`, which checks a policy's claims and not only its method names. `./conformance` also exports `installDiagnosticsGate()`: GTK's failure mode is exit 0, so every vector asserts zero GTK warnings. Adapters: `./solid` over `solid-js/universal` (10 methods), `./vue` over `@vue/runtime-core` (10 required + 4 optional) and `./react` over react-reconciler's HostConfig — three contracts over ONE host, which is what makes framework-agnostic a measured claim rather than a decision. The type surfaces those adapters are written against are generated too: `WidgetPropsByTag`, `JSX.IntrinsicElements` for both JSX dialects, and Vue `GlobalComponents`. What `remove` MEANS differs and was measured both ways: a teardown for Vue (it moves with `insert` alone) and a detach for Solid (one op for both, so its per-node scope disconnects handlers and its disposer tears the tree down). No adapter carries a widget name, a widget VALUE (`new Gtk.Box()`, `instanceof`, `$gtype`, a call — a type annotation is fine), a runtime `gi://` import or an insertion rule, machine-checked by `scripts/check-adapter-import-direction.mjs`, which self-tests 26 fixtures and refuses to run on an empty adapter set. What the adapters used to compensate for is host surface now: `widgetOf`, `isHostElement`, `describeValue`, `withoutKeys`, `createDetachedContainer` (`<KeepAlive>`/`<Suspense>` off-screen storage — the one runtime `gi://` import in any adapter), and `null` reading as REMOVED alongside `undefined`. ONE vector table runs through all three adapters (`conformance/vectors.mts`, a `.mts` so its `@gjsify/unit` edge never ships) over a per-adapter mount/patch/unmount seam — text children, `slot`, `layout` and the `uncurated` refusal, none of which any adapter spec covered; deleting `flushText` reds 12 vectors across three adapters instead of 2 in React alone. `runHostProbeApp` in the main barrel is the showcase self-verification harness (env gate, diagnostics gate, a `check()` recorder that verifies ITSELF, `PROBE: PASS|FAIL <json>`, and the `activate` path structurally), replacing 70 + 68 hand-written lines in the two gtk-host showcases. Vue additionally needs its four production defines or `--globals auto` statically injects DOM polyfills for dev-only branches; a vector asserts `globalThis.document` is undefined.

@gjsify/gtk-runtime-darwin-arm64.note: Prebuilt GTK runtime data bundle for node-gi on macOS arm64 (darwin twin of the win32 bundle). Built by the shared `packages/node-gi/scripts/build-gtk-runtime-darwin.mjs`, which serves both darwin arches: the target is derived from the running Node and `--out` is cross-checked against the destination package's `os`/`cpu`, so a leg cannot write one arch's closure into the other's package. Ships exactly the typelibs it can back: the typelib->library mapping is read from each typelib header (shared `packages/node-gi/scripts/typelib-backers.mjs`), an unbacked typelib is dropped unless a kept one depends on it (then the build FAILS -- `Pango-1.0` needs `HarfBuzz-0.0`, so `libharfbuzz-gobject` is a base seed), and the finished bundle is re-verified off disk against a namespace floor. Third-party terms ship with the binaries (`gtk/licenses/` + `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`, attributed per dylib via its Homebrew keg, incl. the install_name_tool/codesign modification statement). release.yml publishes the `--windowing` superset; display-free stays the conformance variant.

@gjsify/gtk-runtime-darwin-x64.note: Intel-macOS sibling of the arm64 bundle, closing the asymmetry left when node-gi's darwin-x64 addon prebuild shipped without one (an Intel Mac got a loadable addon and still had to `brew install gtk4` by hand). Shares the arm64 package's builder outright; the relocation assertion moved into that script and is brew-prefix-DERIVED, because the literal `/opt/homebrew` is vacuously absent on Intel, where the prefix is /usr/local. Display-free chain only: node-gi.yml's `macos-gtk-runtime` -> `macos-gtk-batteries-included` matrix (runner `macos-15-intel`, never brew-installs GTK, so a green leg IS the batteries-included proof); the `--windowing` GUI pair stays arm64-only (see Open TODOs). Same typelib-symmetry and license-payload rules as the arm64 sibling (one shared builder); release.yml now publishes the `--windowing` superset for both legs.

@gjsify/gtk-runtime-win32-x64.note: Batteries-included GTK runtime for node-gi windowing on Windows: `build-gtk-runtime.mjs --windowing` builds a superset of the display-free bundle carrying gdk-pixbuf loaders + `loaders.cache`, compiled GSettings schemas, Adwaita/hicolor icon themes + caches and Fontconfig; node-gi's loader wires the env off the `gschemas.compiled` marker. Since 0.27.2 the PUBLISHED tarball is that `--windowing` superset (through 0.27.1 release.yml built the display-free variant, so npm carried `windowing:false`/`dataBytes:0` and a `GtkSource-5` typelib with no gtksourceview DLL). Shares the darwin builder rules for typelib symmetry (only backed typelibs ship) and for the license payload, which on a flat gvsbuild prefix is prefix-attributed rather than per-DLL.

@gjsify/http.note: Server (Soup.Server via `@gjsify/http-soup-bridge`, chunked streaming, upgrade event, `SoupMessageLifecycle` per-request helper: GC guard for in-flight Soup messages + `'wrote-chunk'`-driven re-unpause + `'disconnected'`/`'finished'` → req/res `'close'`/`'aborted'`), ClientRequest (Soup.Session, timeout events, auth option, signal option), IncomingMessage (timeout events; close-only-via-destroy per Node semantics), ServerResponse (setTimeout, chunked transfer), OutgoingMessage, `ServerRequestSocket` (Duplex-typed `req.socket` with working pause/resume/destroySoon for Hono backpressure), STATUS_CODES, METHODS, Agent (constructor options, keepAlive, maxSockets, scheduling), validateHeaderName/Value, maxHeaderSize. Known limitation: libsoup stops polling the input stream while a server message is paused, so `'disconnected'` does not fire for long-poll/SSE clients that hang up — see Upstream GJS Patch Candidates. Browser slot `partial` (no inbound TCP; client half rides fetch).

@gjsify/http-soup-bridge.note: Vala/GObject library consumed by `@gjsify/http`. Wraps `Soup.Server` + `SoupServerMessage`, exposing JS only plain GObject classes whose lifetime SpiderMonkey GC cannot race. Solves two libsoup GC crashes: (1) `BoxedBase::finalize → g_source_unref` SIGSEGV from deferred-GC on in-flight Soup messages, (2) `g_main_context_unref` assertion from shared `GMainContext` ref imbalance. Contains `Server` (emits `request-received`/`upgrade`/`error-occurred`), `Request` (read-side snapshot), `Response` (write side, owns `SoupServerMessage` C-side incl. pause/unpause bookkeeping), and a peer-close watcher (`g_socket_create_source(IN|HUP|ERR)` + non-blocking `MSG_PEEK` probe — unreachable from JS because `Gio.Socket.receive_message` is not introspectable).

@gjsify/http2.note: `createServer()` (HTTP/1.1 via Soup; opt-in `allowHTTP1:false` → raw h2c via `Http2NativeDispatcher` on `Gio.SocketService`), `createSecureServer()` (h2 via ALPN + TLS), `connect()` (Soup.Session default, `nativeDispatcher:'force'` for native h2c client + push-event reception), compat layer (`Http2ServerRequest`/`Http2ServerResponse`), session API (`'stream'` event + `ServerHttp2Stream.respond()`), `ClientHttp2Session.request()` → `ClientHttp2Stream`, protocol constants + settings pack/unpack, `respondWithFile()`/`respondWithFD()` (statCheck honoured), `pushStream()`/`createPushResponse()` with wire-level PUSH_PROMISE on the native path (`ERR_HTTP2_NESTED_PUSH` on nested push), client-side `'stream'` event for pushed resources, GOAWAY on `server.close()`, RST_STREAM on `stream.close(code)`, GC-pinning of active `SessionBridge` instances. Two lazy native-dispatcher loads still use a bare `require` (sanctioned lint disables — see Open TODOs).

@gjsify/http2-native.note: Vala/GObject library (+ C shim around `nghttp2_hd_deflate_*`) consumed by `@gjsify/http2` — nghttp2 primitives unreachable through libsoup's GIR API. `FrameEncoder` (HPACK header-block encoder + raw frame builders for DATA/HEADERS/PUSH_PROMISE/SETTINGS/WINDOW_UPDATE/PING/RST_STREAM/GOAWAY), `StreamIdAllocator` (RFC 7540 §5.1.1 even-id sequencer + client-id tracking for GOAWAY), `SessionBridge` (full `nghttp2_session` driver, server + client modes, complete submit family; events drain via `gjsify_http2_event_*` getters and re-emit on the main loop via `GLib.Idle.add()`). Header signals carry `GLib.Variant("a(ss)")` so GJS's marshaller doesn't trip `G_VALUE_HOLDS_POINTER`; all buffer ownership stays C-side via `GLib.Bytes`. @gjsify/https.note: Agent (defaultPort, protocol, maxSockets, destroy, options, keepAlive, scheduling), globalAgent, request (URL/options/headers/timeout/methods), get, createServer, Server. Browser slot `partial` (`TLSSocket`/`createSecureContext` cannot exist — the UA terminates TLS below JS).

@gjsify/iframe.note: HTMLIFrameElement, IFrameBridge → WebKit.WebView, postMessage bridge, navigation (loadUri/loadHtml/goBack/goForward/reload + canGoBack/canGoForward). Ships `/register` for `HTMLIFrameElement` + the `'iframe'` element factory (ADR 0012 — WebKit stays an optional system dep).

@gjsify/inspector.note: Session.post(), open/close; empty. V8-specific, hard to port.

@gjsify/lightningcss-native.note: Vala+Rust cdylib bridge to lightningcss for GJS. `Engine.transform()` (in-memory CSS→CSS) + `Engine.bundle()` (entry file, resolves `@import` chains via lightningcss's FileProvider), browserslist queries accepted directly. Backs `cssAsStringPlugin` under `--app gjs` — `css-as-string` resolves + inlines bare-specifier `@import`s in JS first (its shared `cssBundleResolver`), then routes flattened CSS through `transform()` for the GTK4 lowering; npm `lightningcss` `bundleAsync` fallback when the prebuild is unavailable. @gjsify/lightningcss-wasm.note: WASM-track companion to `lightningcss-native`: vendors `lightningcss-wasm@1.32.0`'s NAPI-on-WASM bundle (15.8 MiB .wasm + napi-wasm runtime + asyncify helper). Decision matrix: 3–5× slower than native on transforms, ~960× slower cold init — kept in tree as a fallback for unsupported architectures.

@gjsify/manifest-conformance.note: The declaration-vs-reality rule registry (portable rules `package-outputs`, `prebuild-artifacts`, `headless`, `field-coverage`; shared context/report/binary-parser libs). Plain committed `lib/*.mjs`, no build — importable from CI scripts with no node_modules. Private/internal today; `gjsify manifest-check` is designed but not shipped (see Open TODOs).

@gjsify/message-channel.note: MessageChannel, MessagePort (W3C, EventTarget-based, transport-pluggable). Stock GJS exposes neither. The pluggable transport hook backs `@gjsify/iframe`'s WebKit bridge and `@gjsify/worker_threads`' cross-process ports.

@gjsify/module.note: builtinModules, isBuiltin (bare/prefixed/subpath/scoped), createRequire (resolve, cache, extensions; ancestor `node_modules` walk; PnP-aware — parses `.pnp.cjs` `RAW_RUNTIME_STATE` directly). Browser slot `partial` (no synchronous CJS loader).

@gjsify/napi.note: N-API host in GJS (ADR 0011) — runs Node's N-API `.node` addons inside GJS by implementing the Node-API C ABI over mozjs-140. Tier 3, own `napi.yml` CI, not a workspace member.
@gjsify/napi.working: Phase 0: full `js_native_api.h` surface + module loader/version/fatal — better-sqlite3 v13 runs unmodified inside GJS, byte-identical to Node, valgrind-clean; conformance oracle every divergence carrying its Phase-0 reason in `conformance/ledger.json`. Phase 1: the tsfn surface (`napi_*_threadsafe_function` + `napi_make_callback` over a thread-safe idle GSource) — `@gjsify/node-gi` itself runs under the shim, byte-identical to native `gi://` across node-gi's whole conformance suite, nothing ledgered (a CI test oracle, NOT a production path). Transparent `.node`→`loadAddon` build integration shipped (`napiNodeAddonPlugin`, always-on for `--app gjs`). Prebuilds: linux-x64 committed + darwin-arm64 CI-built (uploaded per release, `platformsUncommitted`).

@gjsify/native-fs-bridge.note: `readFile`, `writeFile`, `readdir`, `stat`, `mkdir`, `unlink`, `exists` via `java.io.File` (Android) + `NSFileManager` (iOS). Spec tests run on GJS + Node off-device via the `assertNativeScript()` guard.

@gjsify/native-platform.note: `isAndroid`/`isIOS`/`isNativeScript`, `assertNativeScript()`, `platformInfo()` (OS version, SDK level, device model, manufacturer) via `android.os.Build` + `UIDevice`. Keyed on runtime globals only — no `@nativescript/core` value import.

@gjsify/nativescript-vite.note: Vite-8 composer for NativeScript apps: `defineNativescriptConfig()` loads `@nativescript/vite`'s config and fixes the Vite-8/Rolldown incompatibilities at compose time (major-gated: function-alias drop, `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` removal, ns-typescript-check strip), stubs missing framework peers via Node synchronous hooks, applies the SBG bundle-sync fix (stable chunk names + `emptyOutDir`), then spreads `gjsifyNativescript()`. @gjsify/node-gi.note: Axis-5 reverse bridge — GI/GObject runtime for Node: unchanged GJS/GObject-Introspection code runs under Node.js (and Bun/Deno from the same N-API binary). Headless core complete (marshalling incl. OUT/INOUT, toggle-ref GC dance, signals, `GObject.registerClass` incl. custom props/signals/vfuncs + chain-up, boxed/struct access, callbacks, mainloop with the uv-driven auto-pump so a bare `node bundle.mjs` drains Gio async work byte-identically to `gjs -m`); GTK/Cairo layer landed (Adwaita window realizes + renders via GSK; the full Libadwaita storybook renders on Linux + Windows via the `--windowing` GTK runtime bundle); GIMarshallingTests oracle 370 pass / 0 fail; graduated Tier 3→2 per ADR 0005 (2026-07-14), dependency-isolation invariant retained (devDep-only seam). 17 `@gjsify/*` packages run their own suites unchanged on it. Deferred limitations tracked in Open TODOs.

@gjsify/node-runtime-darwin-arm64.note: Bundled Node interpreter for macOS on Apple silicon, so a `gjsify ship` artifact can carry its own where the host provides none. Ships `bin/node` + Node's `LICENSE` and nothing else: the full distribution drags in npm's bundled `node_modules`, 149 further LICENSE files (150 including Node's own, the same count in every archive of the release), for code that is not being shipped. One verbatim `LICENSE` from a release TAG discharges MIT + Apache-2.0 (OpenSSL is upstream 3.5.7, Apache-2.0 alone, so no advertising clause) + BSD-3 + Unicode-3.0 + zlib + Artistic-2.0 + BlueOak-1.0.0 + ISC, with zero copyleft in the binary. Resolved BY NAME by whoever ships the app, no `optionalDependencies` edge — the `@gjsify/gtk-runtime-*` rule; cross-assembling on Linux needs `npm install --force` or `npm pack`, since `os`/`cpu` gating makes a plain install EBADPLATFORM. First publish not yet bootstrapped.

@gjsify/node-runtime-darwin-x64.note: Intel-macOS sibling of the arm64 interpreter bundle, from the same release and the same shared fetcher — nothing in the fetch or the verification is arch-dependent, since the payload is a verified DOWNLOAD rather than a build, which is what lets all three targets publish from one ubuntu job with no macOS and no Windows runner. Same two-file payload, same licence discharge, same by-name resolution. First publish not yet bootstrapped.

@gjsify/node-runtime-win32-x64.note: Windows-x64 interpreter bundle: `bin/node.exe` (the whole runtime — the win-x64 zip contains zero DLLs) + Node's `LICENSE`. ⚠️ Sourced from the `.zip`, never from `https://nodejs.org/dist/<v>/win-x64/`: that directory holds `node.exe`, `node.lib` and debug symbols and NO LICENSE, so the convenient route drops the redistribution obligation with no error — and it is a WINDOWS-only shortcut, the darwin equivalents being 404. The same release also ships the licence twice byte-different (157,609 B LF in the tarballs, 160,555 B CRLF in the zip, 2,946 CR), so the size check is a Set of both. First publish not yet bootstrapped.

Root export pure; side effects in `@gjsify/node-globals/register` (granular subpaths per feature; catch-all kept as the official "give me everything" opt-in). Users opt in via `--globals` (default `auto`) or an explicit register import.

@gjsify/node-polyfills.note: Dep-only umbrella — pulls every Node polyfill so `gjsify create-app` templates and CLI-generated scaffolds resolve any `node:*` import out of the box. No runtime code.

@gjsify/npm-registry.note: fetchPackument (+conditional ETag revalidation), fetchTarball with sha512 SRI verification, parseNpmrc (registries, scoped overrides, `_authToken`, basic auth, env expansion), nerf-dart auth-host normalization, longest-prefix Authorization resolution. Cross-platform via `globalThis.fetch` + `crypto.subtle`.

@gjsify/os.note: homedir, hostname, cpus, platform, arch, type, release, endianness, EOL, devNull, availableParallelism, userInfo, networkInterfaces, constants (signals/errno), loadavg, uptime, memory.

@gjsify/oxfmt-native.note: Vala+Rust cdylib GI bridge to oxc's formatter — the Node-free engine behind `gjsify format`/`fix` under GJS (npm `oxfmt` is a Rust napi binary GJS cannot load). Links the pure-Rust oxfmt CLI core via Cargo path-deps into `refs/oxc`, pinned in lockstep with the npm `oxfmt` devDep (`refs-pin` + `refsLockstep` machine-checked). `Formatter.run(args)` = the full CLI in-process (.oxfmtrc/.editorconfig resolution, ignore handling, --write/--check/--list-different) + single-shot `Formatter.format()`. Not covered (napi-only upstream): the Prettier ExternalFormatter (CSS/HTML/Vue/Markdown), `.oxfmtrc.ts`, --init/--migrate, LSP + stdin.

@gjsify/path.note: POSIX + Win32. Validated on-device on NativeScript V8 (integration suite).

@gjsify/perf_hooks.note: performance (now, timeOrigin, mark/measure, getEntries/ByName/ByType, clearMarks/clearMeasures, toJSON), monitorEventLoopDelay, PerformanceObserver, eventLoopUtilization, timerify.

@gjsify/process.note: EventEmitter-based, env (CRUD, enumerate, coerce; dotenv-validated Proxy traps), cwd/chdir, platform, arch, pid/ppid, version/versions, argv, hrtime/hrtime.bigint (named import preserves `.bigint`), memoryUsage, nextTick (batched GLib-idle delivery keeps GTK input responsive), exit/kill, config, execArgv, cpuUsage, signal handler registration, stdout/stderr write methods, emitWarning; stdin/stdout/stderr as ProcessReadStream/ProcessWriteStream (isTTY, setRawMode, columns/rows via `@gjsify/terminal-native` or env/GLib fallback); SIGWINCH → stdout/stderr 'resize'.

@gjsify/react-native.note: React Native's export surface over @gjsify/gtk-host (ADR 0032). The support table in `src/support-table.ts` carries a status and a reason for all 92 names react-native publicly exports; the bundler gate, the runtime refusals and the generated README all read the same file.
@gjsify/react-native.missing: P2 and P3: the list family (FlatList/SectionList over Gtk.ListView), Image, the Touchable family, Dimensions, Alert, Animated. `StyleSheet` (React Native's own, not the generated sheet) is still P1 and unbuilt. `Modal` stays refused for a measured reason rather than a scheduling one: an Adw.Dialog is presented against a parent and never parented by it, and `box.append(dialog)` calls g_error() — SIGABRT, not a catchable exception — so it needs a portal seam in the host. Implemented: all three layers, seven P1 primitives, four P1 APIs, AppRegistry/registerRootComponent over @gjsify/adwaita-app, EventEmitter, unstable_batchedUpdates. Every other name resolves to a value that refuses with the table's own sentence. ADR 0032 § 11's regression proof is `showcases/gtk/rn-design-system`: a design-system layer (badge, button, card, chip, rule, rail, screen, section header, thumbnail, typography) written fresh under MIT against the same class vocabulary, whose probe asserts which widget each primitive became, which `css-classes` landed and what the generated rule behind each one says, and zero GTK diagnostics. It is what found the `GStrv` write defect that made every styled node un-re-renderable (`writeProperty` in gtk-host).

@gjsify/readline.note: Interface (lifecycle, line events, mixed line endings, Unicode, chunked input, long lines, history), question (sequential, output), prompt, pause/resume, async iterator, clearLine/clearScreenDown/cursorTo/moveCursor, readline/promises, `Interface[Symbol.dispose]` = close() (`using`).

@gjsify/resolve-npm.note: Central alias registry: the curated `ALIASES_*` tables per target, the globals map (`GJS_GLOBALS_MAP`/groups/METHOD_MARKERS closure data), derived runtime-slot routing (`withDerivedSlotRouting` composing `package.json#gjsify.runtimes` under the curated baseline), the pnp-relay helper, and the committed register-globals closure map. Plain `lib/*.mjs`, no build.

@gjsify/rolldown-native.note: Vala+Rust cdylib bridge to rolldown — the DEFAULT bundler engine under GJS (npm rolldown is a Rust N-API addon GJS cannot load; `bundler-pick.ts` selects native under GJS, npm under Node, `GJSIFY_BUNDLER` override). Wraps `rolldown::Bundler::generate()` in a per-call current-thread tokio runtime, JSON options/output at the FFI boundary; `bundleWithPlugins()` drives a `BundlerSession` GObject running all 12 rolldown hook positions, so gjsify's full JS plugin set runs on the native engine; `runNativeBundle` replicates npm rolldown's `.write()` incl. nested chunk/asset dirs. Built from the `refs/rolldown` submodule via cargo path-dep, pinned in exact lockstep with the npm `rolldown` devDep (`check-refs-pin.mjs`). Portable anonymous-pipe wakeup channel; `gjsify.platforms` declares all four of linux-x64/linux-arm64/darwin-arm64/darwin-x64 and the darwin artifacts are committed. What no CI leg covers is the NODE-FREE path those prebuilds exist for — both darwin suites drive the CLI under Node (see Open TODOs). No watch/HMR (`--watch` needs npm rolldown under Node) and no incremental builds. A plugin hook's `moduleType` covers only js/ecmascript/json/text — `parse_module_type` in `plugin_proxy.rs` rejects `ts`/`tsx`/`jsx` and the rest of rolldown's `ModuleType`, so a plugin that compiles a foreign extension INTO TypeScript builds under Node and fails under GJS (see Open TODOs).

@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-deepkit.note: Deepkit TypeScript runtime reflection via `@deepkit/type-compiler` (`transform` hook, `order: 'pre'`, lazy-loaded). Opt-in only (`reflection: false` default) — it transforms TS `extends` method definitions into invalid syntax on non-Deepkit code, so it stays off unless a project uses Deepkit runtime types.

@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-gjsify.note: Platform orchestration for `gjsify build`: the `--app gjs|node|browser|nativescript` target factories, externals policy, alias plugin, auto-globals detection (acorn on post-tree-shake output), process-stub/wellknown-symbols banner, css-as-string (lightningcss), text/dataurl loaders, blueprint composition, `gjsGiNodePlugin` (gi://→node-gi rewrite), `napiNodeAddonPlugin` (transparent `.node` addon loading), unresolved-workspace-import guard, gjs/node bundle guards, platform-resolve + platform-defines for NativeScript, `./runtime` host-detection subpath.

@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-pnp.note: Yarn PnP resolver + relay through the polyfill meta-packages (`getPnpPlugin` with `transformContentsFactory`), so external consumers under PnP resolve every transitive `@gjsify/*` register subpath without re-declaring them.

@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-solid.missing: No `<style>`/CSS handling and no dev/HMR mode: the plugin is the COMPILE step only. `generate: "dom"` and `"ssr"` are settable and only shallowly tested — nothing in this repo has a DOM to render into, so the `dom` case is asserted on the emitted code and never run. The lazy-load claim holds on the Node CLI path; under GJS the CLI bundles this plugin to one file before importing it, so a project that declares the plugin parses Babel's ~3.4 MB on every build even when no module matches.
@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-solid.note: Solid JSX for Rolldown: `babel-preset-solid` in `generate: "universal"` mode with `moduleName: "@gjsify/gtk-host/solid"`, wired through `package.json#gjsify.bundler.plugins`. Babel and not oxc because Solid's JSX is a COMPILER, not a runtime, and no oxc port of `babel-plugin-jsx-dom-expressions` exists — pointed at a `.tsx` with no JSX configuration Rolldown's own transformer defaults to the automatic React runtime, emits `import { jsx } from "react/jsx-runtime"`, reports the unresolved import as a WARNING and exits 0. Babel is lazy-loaded on the first matching module (the `@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-deepkit` contract), and the cache holds the compiler MODULES rather than the assembled preset chain — caching the chain made `moduleName` and `generate` inert for every plugin instance after the first in a process. Preset order follows Solid's own tooling (Babel applies presets last-to-first, so `@babel/preset-typescript` is listed second and runs first); measured on 14 inputs chosen to break it, both orders emit byte-identical output, so the order is convention here and not a constraint. `src/plugin.spec.ts` runs on Node AND GJS, which is what holds the claim that Babel loads under GJS at all — the primary target for these bundles. The compiler emits the renderer op names LITERALLY, so the target module must re-export every member of Solid's `Renderer<NodeType>` under its contract name.

@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-vue.missing: No `<style>` handling and no dev/HMR mode: the plugin is the COMPILE step only, and a `<style>` block is REFUSED by name rather than dropped (GTK styling is a `Gtk.CssProvider` concern). `<script lang="jsx"|"tsx">` is refused too — `resolveId` picks the module id's extension before anything has read the file, so one suffix is all there is. A split SFC (`<template src>`, `<script src>`) and a `<template lang>` other than `html` are refused by name as well, and so is every DOM-only template feature (`v-show`, `v-model` on an element, an event MODIFIER, `v-html`, `v-text`, `class`/`style` in both spellings, `<Transition>`/`<TransitionGroup>`) — all of them compile on `@vue/compiler-dom` and then fail at exit 0, so refusing is the feature, not a gap. Asset-URL rewriting, custom blocks, SSR, `?query` suffixes and watch-mode dependency registration are all out of scope; a custom block is the one thing neither compiled nor refused, and it is named on stderr through the plugin context. `load` now returns a real source map, but gjsify's own build presets set `output.sourcemap: false` AFTER spreading the caller's output options, so under `gjsify build --app <target>` it is not written — it reaches a consumer through a plain Rolldown/Vite config. `moduleType` on a transform result is the mechanism this plugin CANNOT use: `@gjsify/rolldown-native` rejects everything but js/ecmascript/json/text (see Open TODOs).
@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-vue.note: Vue 3 single-file components for Rolldown: `@vue/compiler-sfc` with `isCustomElement` accepting BOTH tag spellings, `runtimeModuleName: "@vue/runtime-core"`, and `hoistStatic: false` as the Vue adapter prescribes, wired through `package.json#gjsify.bundler.plugins`. Compiler loaded lazily on the first `.vue` module (the `@gjsify/rolldown-plugin-deepkit` contract), and `@vue/compiler-sfc` loads under GJS as-is — no CJS-callable defect, unlike `@babel/helper-module-imports` in the Solid sibling. Six measurements are load-bearing and each is pinned by a test: (1) without `isCustomElement` all 7 tags of a fixture compiled to `_resolveComponent(...)` and ZERO element vnodes; (2) the predicate is consulted for PascalCase too, so a kebab-only rule leaves `<GtkBox>` type-checking and then resolving as a missing component; (3) `isCustomElement` and `comments` are PARSE-time options — setting them in `compilerOptions` while reusing `descriptor.template.ast` is a silent no-op, and that no-op faked its own A/B because `compileTemplate` re-parses an already-TRANSFORMED ast; (4) `runtimeModuleName` reaches `compileScript` only through `templateOptions`, or the script half imports `vue` and pulls in `@vue/runtime-dom`; (5) `comments: false` must be pinned in `compilerOptions` AS WELL as in `templateParseOptions`, or the plugin is non-deterministic WITHIN one process — `parse()` LRU-caches the descriptor, so the second compile of one file takes `resolveTemplateAST`, which re-parses `inAST.source` with `compilerOptions` as the parse options: measured, pass 1 emitted 0 `createCommentVNode` calls and pass 2 emitted 1; (6) `transformHoist: null` was DEAD — compiler-dom's `compile()` spreads its own `transformHoist: stringifyStatic` after the caller's options, and `null` vs `undefined` produced byte-identical output; only `hoistStatic: false` suppresses the stringifier. Every DOM-only template feature is refused BY NAME with what to write on GTK instead, through one `nodeTransform`: the absent `@vue/runtime-core` exports (`vShow`, `vModelText`, `withModifiers`, `withKeys`, `Transition`) are a rolldown MISSING_EXPORT WARNING at exit 0, and the dead DOM props (`class`, `style`, `innerHTML`, `textContent`) are an `unknown-prop` refusal at RENDER time inside a GLib callback — also exit 0. `v-model` is refused on an ELEMENT only, because on a component it compiles to `modelValue`/`onUpdate:modelValue` and imports nothing DOM-shaped. `load` hands rolldown one map over the whole `.vue` file, built by decoding and re-encoding both halves' maps rather than splicing their `mappings` strings — the generated column resets per line but source index/line/column are deltas carried across the whole map. The module id gains a `.gjsify-vue.ts` suffix in `resolveId` because that is the ONLY mechanism measured working on both bundler engines, and an EXTERNAL resolution is handed back verbatim instead (renaming it minted a virtual id whose `load` then ENOENT'd). 193 tests on Node and GJS; the end-to-end guard is `showcases/gtk/vue-host-counter`, whose build, self-asserting probe and `check-vue-program.mjs` type gate all run in CI — and which is measurably blind to three of the settings above, which is why this package has a suite of its own.

@gjsify/semver.note: Pure-JS subset of node-semver: SemVer, Range, satisfies, maxSatisfying, minSatisfying, validRange; caret/tilde/hyphen/x/star ranges, OR sets, prerelease comparison, npm prerelease-range gating.

@gjsify/sqlite.note: node:sqlite over the libgda SQLite provider (`gi://Gda?version=6.0`).

@gjsify/string_decoder.note: UTF-8, Base64, hex, streaming; pure manual UTF-8 decoder implementing the W3C maximal-subpart algorithm.

@gjsify/tar.note: Streaming `.tar`/`.tar.gz` reader: ustar headers + PAX extended (path/linkpath/size), GNU long-name (L) + long-link (K), checksum-validated. `extractTarball()` strips the npm `package/` prefix, preserves modes, creates symlinks, refuses entries escaping destDir.

@gjsify/terminal-native.note: Optional Vala prebuild: `GjsifyTerminal.Terminal.is_tty(fd)` (Posix.isatty), `get_size(fd)` (ioctl TIOCGWINSZ), `set_raw_mode(fd, enable)` (termios — clears ICANON+ECHO+ISIG, Node-parity so Ctrl-C is a keystroke, not SIGINT); `ResizeWatcher` with a `resized(rows, cols)` signal on SIGWINCH via `GLib.Unix.signal_add()`. @gjsify/timers.note: setTimeout/setInterval/setImmediate (delay verification, args, clear, ordering) + timers/promises. GLib-source-safe: replaces setTimeout/setInterval with `GLib.timeout_add` to avoid the SM-GC race on GLib.Source BoxedInstances; Node-shaped `GjsifyTimeout` wrapper with no-op ref/unref/hasRef, working refresh/Symbol.dispose/Symbol.toPrimitive.

@gjsify/tls.note: TLSSocket via Gio.TlsClientConnection: getPeerCertificate (Node shape incl. `detailed=true` issuer-chain walk), getProtocol, getCipher, ALPN advertise/negotiate, servername; connect (mTLS via `set_certificate`, custom CA validation, custom `checkServerIdentity`); createServer/TLSServer (requestCert+rejectUnauthorized, addContext/SNICallback with real ClientHello-driven server-side SNI via BufferedInputStream peek + RFC 6066 §3 parser, ALPN); createSecureContext (string/Buffer/Uint8Array/array PEM, ca bundle); checkServerIdentity (full RFC 6125 §6.4.3 incl. wildcard rules, A-label matching, `ERR_TLS_CERT_ALTNAME_INVALID`); getCiphers, DEFAULT_CIPHERS, DEFAULT_MIN/MAX_VERSION, rootCertificates. Phase 2 session access via `@gjsify/tls-native`: `getFinished()`/`getPeerFinished()`/`getSession()`/`setSession()`/`isSessionReused()` + `'session'` event + `{session}` option, `tls-unique`/`tls-exporter` channel binding auto-selected per TLS version; `hasTlsSessionAccess()` gate. OCSP-response parsing surfaced via `parseOcspResponse`/`hasOcspSupport`.

@gjsify/tls-native.note: Optional Vala prebuild for GnuTLS capabilities Gio does not expose. Phase 1: OCSP-response parsing — sibling `gnutls-ocsp.vapi` fills the OCSP gap in Vala 0.56's `gnutls.vapi`; `Tls.parse_ocsp_response(uint8[])` returns an `OcspResponseInfo` GObject (all RFC 6960 §4.2.1 fields). Phase 2 (Path A, functional): `SessionAccess` + `ChannelBindingType` wrap a `Gio.TlsConnection` — is_supported/for_connection/is_session_reused/get_session_data/set_session_data/get_channel_binding/get_finished/get_peer_finished — via the C shim `src/c/gjsify-tls-private.{c,h}`, which extracts `gnutls_session_t` from `GTlsConnectionGnutls`'s private struct (layout vendored from refs/glib-networking, stable across 2.74–2.84) and force-loads the GIO TLS module. Loaded via `imports.gi.GjsifyTls` with try/catch — safe when the typelib is not installed.

@gjsify/tsc.note: Bundled-toolchain axis exemplar: upstream `typescript`'s `_tsc.js` CLI wrapped into a GJS bundle (`dist/tsc.gjs.mjs`, `gjsify-tsc` bin — a build output since ADR 0002, shipped in the tarball rather than committed) pinned to the workspace TS invariant (`TYPESCRIPT_VERSION`). The workspace SELF-HOSTS its type-checking (`check` = `gjsify tsc --noEmit`) and `.d.ts` emit (`build:types`) on it — byte-identical to node tsc, ~1.3× at full-workspace scale. Ships the ~108 version-locked `lib*.d.ts` (committed; `pickLibSource()` keep/refresh/error logic guards against a stale or partial installed `typescript`).

@gjsify/tty.note: ReadStream/WriteStream, isatty (Posix or GLib fallback), ANSI escapes, clearLine, cursorTo, getColorDepth (env-based), hasColors, getWindowSize (ioctl or env/default fallback), setRawMode (termios or no-op fallback) — all terminal primitives via `@gjsify/terminal-native` when installed.

@gjsify/unit.note: Test framework (describe/it/expect, cross-platform Node+GJS+browser) + vitest-compat surface (`vi.fn`/`stubGlobal`/`stubEnv`, `toMatchObject`/`toBeNaN`/`toHaveBeenCalled*`, `expect().rejects.toThrow`/`.resolves.toResolve`), `browserSignalDone` for the Playwright axis, fail-count isolation (a leaked late assertion becomes a distinct stray, never poisons a bystander `it()`), and callback-assertion attribution: an `expect` thrown from a host callback off the awaited chain is charged to the test that armed it instead of ending the run (`uncaughtException` hook on the Node family) or timing out anonymously (assertion ledger on GJS).

@gjsify/url.note: URL (with static `URL.createObjectURL`/`revokeObjectURL` over `Blob._tmpPath` + `file://`), URLSearchParams via GLib.Uri.

@gjsify/util.note: inspect (colors, styles, custom symbol, defaultOptions), format (%%, %s/%d/%j/%i/%f), promisify (custom symbol), callbackify, deprecate, inherits (`super_`), isDeepStrictEqual, styleText, stripVTControlCharacters, types (isDate/RegExp/Map/Set/Promise/ArrayBuffer/TypedArray/Async/Generator/WeakMap/WeakSet/DataView), TextEncoder/TextDecoder.

@gjsify/utils.note: Shared GJS utilities: Gio wrappers, process info, encoding, `ensureMainLoop`/`quitMainLoop`, structuredClone polyfill, `installCriticalLogWriter`. Declares `node: "polyfill"` but re-exports `@gjsify/webaudio` (`node: "none"`) — flagged on every audit run, see Open TODOs.

@gjsify/web-streams.note: ReadableStream (incl. `type:'bytes'`), WritableStream, TransformStream, ReadableByteStreamController + `autoAllocateChunkSize`, ReadableStreamBYOBReader (`read(view, {min?})` preserves view-constructor), ReadableStreamBYOBRequest, polymorphic close/error/cancel for default + BYOB readers, byte-stream `tee()`, TextEncoderStream, TextDecoderStream, ByteLengthQueuingStrategy, CountQueuingStrategy (WHATWG Streams polyfill for GJS).

No runtime branching — decode + playback run on gjs AND the node-gi reverse bridge (node/bun/deno; bun/deno need the context pump, see Open TODOs).

@gjsify/webcrypto.note: SubtleCrypto (digest, AES-CBC/CTR/GCM, AES-KW (RFC 3394), HMAC, ECDSA, RSA-PSS, RSA-OAEP, PBKDF2, HKDF, ECDH, generateKey, importKey/exportKey, deriveBits/deriveKey, wrapKey/unwrapKey), CryptoKey, getRandomValues, randomUUID. Owns the workspace entropy chain: `@gjsify/webcrypto/random` (leaf subpath) exports `fillRandomBytes()` with an ordered, reported source chain (WebCrypto → /dev/urandom via Gio → GLib.random_int_range → Math.random; the last two warn once) + `isSecureRandomSource(tier)`.

@gjsify/webgl.note: WebGLRenderingContext (1.0), WebGL2RenderingContext (2.0 — overrides texImage2D/texSubImage2D/drawElements for GLES3.2 compat, native FBO completeness delegation, GLSL 1.0 compat for versionless shaders, clearBufferfv/iv/uiv/fi, premultipliedAlpha), HTMLCanvasElement (GTK-backed; `width`/`height` report the DRAWING BUFFER in device pixels — allocation × scale-factor — while `clientWidth`/`offset*` stay logical CSS pixels), WebGLBridge (Gtk.GLArea subclass, rAF, resize re-render, eager context init, `installGlobals()` publishes `devicePixelRatio` as a live accessor over the widget scale factor), extensions — via the gwebgl Vala bridge (prebuild). Context methods split into focused `src/ts/context/` modules with prototype-merge install functions. Ships `/register` for the WebGL context classes (ADR 0012). Deferred items: see the WebGL known-issues section below.

@gjsify/webkit-native.note: Apple WebKit (WKWebView) behind a GObject API shaped like WebKitGTK 6.0 — the darwin backend for @gjsify/iframe (ADR 0022). Contains no JavaScript: one Objective-C library whose typelib deliberately claims the `WebKit-6.0` namespace, so @gjsify/iframe keeps `gi://WebKit?version=6.0` verbatim and carries no OS branch. Exposes WebView (a derivable Gtk.Widget presenting the offscreen WKWebView as a GdkTexture via takeSnapshot — 15.8 ms at 1024x768 on a GPU-less Intel VM, a ~63 fps ceiling), UserContentManager, UserScript (boxed, matching WebKitUserScript so `new WebKit.UserScript(...)` keeps working), Settings, the load-changed/LoadEvent lifecycle, the script-message-received postMessage bridge, evaluate_javascript() and get_snapshot(). Ships a CFRunLoop drain source without which none of it runs: WKWebView delivers through a CFRunLoop and a GMainContext does not pump one (docs/poc/webkit-runloop-darwin.m). Forwards mouse, scroll and keyboard from the GTK widget by re-synthesizing NSEvents (no window and no responder chain are needed, and the event location is bottom-left even though WKWebView is flipped — docs/poc/webkit-input-darwin.m). Named script worlds and user-script allow/block URL patterns are honoured; the first ADR revision wrongly called WKContentWorld nonexistent, so meson now pins -mmacosx-version-min=11.0. NOT implemented: document.hasFocus() is always false (no window to derive it from, measured) and the pointer cursor never changes; App Sandbox is unanswered while the hardened runtime works; darwin-arm64 is built and uploaded on every ci:macos run but not yet committed.

@gjsify/webview2-native.note: Microsoft WebView2 (Chromium) behind a GObject API shaped like WebKitGTK 6.0 — the win32 backend for @gjsify/iframe (ADR 0035), stage 1. DEMONSTRATED on windows-latest, not merely built: the win32 load test (scripts/probe-win32.mjs, through node-gi built from source against the same gvsbuild bundle) passes 13 assertions in 7.18 s against a 60 s deadline — gi://WebKit 6.0 resolves, `new WebKit.WebView()` is a Gtk.Widget reporting HostingMode.OVERLAY, the Win32 message-pump GSource reports ATTACHED, load_html() reaches LoadEvent.FINISHED (events [0,2,3]), evaluate_javascript() reads a marker back OUT OF THE DOM, get_snapshot() returns a 640x480 texture encoding to 5966 B of PNG, script-message-received carries the page's own postMessage, and all five divergence warnings fire. The artifact is also gated for redistribution: the typelib records a .dll leaf, the DLL links the redistributable CRT (import table read with dumpbin, not by loading it — windows-latest HAS Visual Studio) and imports no WebView2Loader.dll. On Fedora, every PR: the portable C compiles, g-ir-scanner runs its dumper, probe-types.js passes 24 assertions under gjs, check-def-exports 34/34, and check-include-paths + check-glib-constants hold the two defect classes that only src/cpp/ could hide. Contains no JavaScript: one library whose typelib deliberately claims the `WebKit-6.0` namespace, so @gjsify/iframe keeps `gi://WebKit?version=6.0` verbatim and carries no OS branch on any of the three operating systems. STAGE 1 IS HOSTED, NOT COMPOSITED by design: the content is a child HWND the OS composites above the GTK surface, so clipping, overdraw, opacity and transforms do not work at all — reported by WebKit.WebView.get_hosting_mode() and get_overlay_constraints() rather than by a doc comment. WHAT IS STILL UNPROVEN: the HOSTED PATH ITSELF. The probe never presents a toplevel (an SSH session on Windows lands in session 0, where present() dies with 0xC0000005), so everything green above ran against the hidden parking window — re-parenting the child HWND under a real GTK toplevel, bounds tracking in device pixels, hiding on unmap, and the claim that input, focus and accessibility come from the OS are all untested. The overlay-constraint reporter has been measured firing by hand on Fedora but CI asserts only the empty case. NOT implemented: stage 2 (composition hosting + Windows.Graphics.Capture into a Gdk.Texture), the .msi's Evergreen-runtime declaration (ADR 0035 decision 5), user-script allow/block URL patterns (refused with a warning rather than injected unfiltered), named script worlds (ignored, warned from every entry point that takes one), SnapshotRegion.FULL_DOCUMENT (returns the viewport, warned), SnapshotOptions other than NONE (ignored, warned), enable-write-console-messages-to-stdout (not honoured, warned) and Settings.allow-file-access-from-file-urls (removed: it reached nothing).

@gjsify/webrtc.note: Full W3C WebRTC (Phases 1–4): RTCPeerConnection (offer/answer, ICE trickle, STUN/TURN config, addTransceiver/addTrack/removeTrack, getStats, restartIce, setConfiguration), RTCDataChannel (string + binary, bufferedAmount, binaryType), RTCRtpSender/Receiver/Transceiver, MediaStream, MediaStreamTrack (GStreamer source integration, enabled→valve), getUserMedia (pipewiresrc/pulsesrc/v4l2src fallback chain), MediaDevices, RTCDTMFSender, RTCCertificate, RTCDtlsTransport/RTCIceTransport/RTCSctpTransport, RTCStatsReport (GstStructure → W3C camelCase), RTCIceCandidate, RTCSessionDescription. Outgoing pipeline source→valve→convert→encode(opus/vp8)→payloader→capsfilter→webrtcbin; end-to-end bidirectional audio verified. Requires GStreamer ≥ 1.20 with gst-plugins-bad + libnice-gstreamer. Detailed phase/deviation notes: see the WebRTC status section below.

@gjsify/webrtc-native.note: Vala/GObject library consumed by `@gjsify/webrtc`. Three main-thread signal bridges — `WebrtcbinBridge` (webrtcbin's `on-negotiation-needed`/`on-ice-candidate`/`on-data-channel` + `notify::*-state`), `DataChannelBridge` (GstWebRTCDataChannel's open/close/error/message/buffered-amount-low + `notify::ready-state`; wraps incoming channels eagerly on the streaming thread so early messages are not dropped), `PromiseBridge` (`Gst.Promise.new_with_change_func`).
